q.t: The four angles of a quadrilateral add up to:
q.e: A diagonal cuts it into two triangles, each with 180°.

q.t: How many sides does a quadrilateral have?
q.e: ‘Quadri’ means four and ‘lateral’ means side.

q.t: How many diagonals does a quadrilateral have?
q.e: One for each pair of opposite vertices.

q.t: Three angles of a quadrilateral are 80°, 90° and 100°. Find the fourth (in degrees).
A quadrilateral with all sides equal and every angle 90° is a:
q.e: A rhombus has equal sides, a rectangle has right angles; a square has both.

q.t: A quadrilateral with exactly one pair of parallel sides is a:
q.e: A parallelogram has two pairs of parallel sides; a trapezium has only one.

q.t: How many vertices does a quadrilateral have?
q.e: One at each corner where two sides meet.

q.t: Two sides of a quadrilateral that share a vertex are called:
q.e: Adjacent means next to each other.

q.t: A quadrilateral in which both pairs of opposite sides are parallel is a:
q.e: That is the definition of a parallelogram.

q.t: A kite has:
o: Two pairs of equal adjacent sides
Two pairs of equal opposite sides
q.e: In a kite the equal sides are next to each other, not opposite.

q.t: The angles of a quadrilateral are in the ratio 3 : 4 : 5 : 6. Find the largest (in degrees).
q.e: 18 parts make 360°, so one part is 20° and the largest is 120°.

q.t: Three angles of a quadrilateral are 75° each. Find the fourth (in degrees).
The angles of a quadrilateral are x°, (x + 10)°, (x + 20)° and (x + 30)°. Find x.
One angle of a quadrilateral is 120° and the other three are equal. Find each of them (in degrees).
q.e: The other three share 240° equally.

q.t: The angles of a quadrilateral are in the ratio 1 : 2 : 3 : 4. Find the smallest (in degrees).
q.e: 10 parts make 360°, so one part is 36°.

q.t: In a convex quadrilateral, the diagonals lie:
q.e: Convex means no corner points inwards, so every diagonal stays inside.

q.t: Two angles of a quadrilateral are 70° and 110°, and the other two are equal. Find each (in degrees).
q.e: The remaining 180° is shared equally.

q.t: The angles of a quadrilateral are (2x + 5)°, (3x − 5)°, (x + 20)° and (4x − 10)°. Find x.
The exterior angles of a quadrilateral (one at each vertex) add up to:
q.e: The exterior angles of every convex polygon total one full turn.

q.t: Three angles of a quadrilateral are 90° each. The quadrilateral must be a:
o: Rhombus that is not a square
q.e: The fourth angle is 360 − 270 = 90°, so all four are right angles.

q.t: In quadrilateral ABCD, ∠C = 100° and ∠D = 60°. The bisectors of ∠A and ∠B meet at P. Find ∠APB (in degrees).
q.e: ∠A + ∠B = 360 − 160 = 200°, so their halves add to 100°. In △APB the third angle is 180 − 100 = 80° — half of (∠C + ∠D).

q.t: Three angles of a quadrilateral are in the ratio 1 : 2 : 3 and the fourth is 120°. Find the largest of the three (in degrees).
q.e: The three share 360 − 120 = 240°. 6 parts → 40° each, so the largest is 120°.

q.t: In a quadrilateral, ∠A = ∠B + 20°, ∠C = ∠B + 40° and ∠D = ∠B + 60°. Find ∠D (in degrees).
Two adjacent angles of a quadrilateral add up to 150°. The other two are in the ratio 3 : 4. Find the larger of these (in degrees).
q.e: The other two share 210°: 7 parts of 30°, so 90° and 120°.

q.t: In kite ABCD, AB = AD and CB = CD. ∠B = 110° and ∠A = 60°. Find ∠C (in degrees).
q.e: The kite is symmetric about AC, so ∠D = ∠B = 110°. Then ∠C = 360 − 220 − 60 = 80.

q.t: In trapezium ABCD, AB ∥ DC, ∠A = 65° and ∠B = 85°. Find ∠C (in degrees).
q.e: BC is a transversal of the parallel sides, so ∠B + ∠C = 180°: ∠C = 95.

q.t: In an isosceles trapezium, each base angle on the longer parallel side is 70°. Find each angle on the shorter parallel side (in degrees).
q.e: Angles on the same leg between the parallel sides are co-interior: 180 − 70 = 110.

q.t: Can all four angles of a quadrilateral be acute?
o: No — they would add up to less than 360°
q.e: Four angles each under 90° total less than 360°, but the sum must be exactly 360°.

q.t: A concave quadrilateral has:
q.e: One vertex is pushed inwards, making a reflex angle there. The total is still 360°.

q.t: At one vertex of a quadrilateral the exterior angle is 70°. Find the interior angle there (in degrees).
q.e: Interior + exterior = 180°.

q.t: In quadrilateral ABCD, ∠A + ∠B = 220°. The bisectors of ∠C and ∠D meet at O. Find ∠COD (in degrees).
q.e: ∠C + ∠D = 140°, halves add to 70°, so ∠COD = 180 − 70 = 110° — half of (∠A + ∠B).

q.t: The angles of a quadrilateral are (x + 20)°, (x − 20)°, (2x + 5)° and (2x − 5)°. Find the largest angle (in degrees).
q.e: 6x = 360, so x = 60. The angles are 80°, 40°, 125° and 115°.

q.t: Three exterior angles of a quadrilateral are 2x°, 3x° and 4x°, and the fourth is 90°. Find the smallest INTERIOR angle (in degrees).
q.e: 9x + 90 = 360, so x = 30. The largest exterior angle is 120°, so the smallest interior angle is 60°.

q.t: In a quadrilateral, ∠A + ∠C = 200° and ∠B = 3 × ∠D. Find ∠B (in degrees).
In kite ABCD, AB = AD and CB = CD. ∠A = 90° and ∠C = 50°. Find ∠B (in degrees).
q.e: ∠B = ∠D by symmetry, and together they make 360 − 140 = 220°.

q.t: In trapezium ABCD, AB ∥ DC and ∠A : ∠D = 2 : 3. Find ∠D (in degrees).
q.e: ∠A + ∠D = 180° (co-interior). 5 parts → 36° each, so ∠D = 108°.

q.t: The four angles of a quadrilateral are consecutive multiples of 12. Find the largest (in degrees).
The bisectors of the four angles of a parallelogram (not a rhombus) enclose a:
q.e: Adjacent angles add to 180°, so their bisectors meet at 90°. Four right angles make a rectangle.

q.t: For a convex quadrilateral, what is the sum of ALL its interior and exterior angles (one exterior at each vertex), in degrees?
q.e: Each vertex contributes interior + exterior = 180°. Four vertices: 720°.

q.t: In quadrilateral ABCD, AB ∥ DC and AD ∥ BC. ∠A = (3x + 10)° and ∠B = (2x + 20)°. Find ∠C (in degrees).
q.e: It is a parallelogram: ∠A + ∠B = 180 gives 5x + 30 = 180, x = 30. ∠C = ∠A = 100°.
